summary: This clipped Federal Reserve Financial Services page gives guidance for organizations depositing and ordering U.S. currency through FedCash Services. It covers a USCP strap band packaging update, which deposits Federal Reserve Banks accept or refuse, currency deposit quality standards, cross-shipping fees and the Recirculation Policy, and normal weekly frequency of cash service. The navigation menus and boilerplate were ignored, and the note ends mid-sentence.
one_line: Federal Reserve guidance on depositing and ordering U.S. currency through FedCash Services, including deposit standards and cross-shipping fees.
key_facts: The United States Currency Program (USCP) is made up of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and the Bureau of Engraving and Printing (BEP).
The USCP is transitioning strap bands of newly produced notes so that all BEP strap bands state the same language and no longer specify denomination, manufacturing equipment source and sequencing.
Federal Reserve Banks accept only genuine U.S. currency for deposit and do not accept foreign currency, mutilated currency, or counterfeit or unlawfully altered currency.
Organizations should forward counterfeit or unlawfully altered currency directly to their local U.S. Secret Service office.
If Federal Reserve Banks detect counterfeit or unlawfully altered currency in a deposit, it is forwarded to the Secret Service and the organization is charged for the difference.
Currency must be bundled by denomination in ten equal straps of 100 notes each, and a full bag may not contain more than 16 bundles.
$1 through $20 denominations must be deposited in full bundles, while $50 and $100 denominations may be deposited in full straps or full bundles.
Banding material must be between 1.00 and 1.57 inches wide, with an approximate weight of 100g/sqm, and made of paper rather than synthetic materials.

Each band must be stamped with the organization's name, ABA routing number, the four-digit endpoint number of the depositing office, the dollar amount, initials or names of verifiers, and the date of validation.

A cross-shipping fee is charged to organizations that deposit fit $10 or $20 notes and then order the same denomination, above a de minimis amount, during the same business week within a Federal Reserve Bank Zone or Sub-zone.
Under the Federal Reserve's Recirculation Policy, organizations should avoid cross-shipping or plan for payment of a Recirculation Fee when cross-shipping is necessary.
For each endpoint, normal cash service is one deposit and one order of currency per week.
The Federal Reserve Bank may, at its discretion, reduce cash orders to maintain currency inventories.
